sections.h2: Ways to sell in Mountlake Terrace
sections.html:
Mountlake Terrace owners choose between a listing, a direct sale and a cash purchase by a buyer who accepts the house untouched. Whichever it is, you finish with a deed, an excise tax affidavit and a recording at Snohomish County.

The city is a suburb on the southern edge of Snohomish County, beside Shoreline and Lynnwood and about 13 miles north of downtown Seattle on Interstate 5. It has an estimated 25,430 residents as of July 1, 2025, packed into 4.06 square miles of land.

sections.h2: Why so many houses date to the 1950s
sections.html:
Developers bought a disused World War II landing field in 1949 and named the project Mountlake Terrace for its plateau setting. Work on the first 250 homes began in June 1949, using a simple two-bedroom plan of 20 by 30 feet, and the first ones were priced from $4,999. Larger homes followed to the north and east, and many early houses were later renovated and expanded.

If you own one of those early houses, expect a buyer's inspector to look hard at additions, wiring and plumbing, and expect questions about whether the remodels were permitted. The city incorporated on November 29, 1954.

The transit station, which opened in 2009, has 890 parking stalls and has been served by Link light rail since the extension to Lynnwood opened in August 2024. Community Transit runs local routes to Edmonds, Lynnwood and Brier, and King County Metro serves the station from Shoreline, Lake Forest Park and Kenmore. Interstate 5 has interchanges at State Route 104, 236th Street Southwest and 220th Street Southwest.

The city's planning map has six neighborhoods, including Town Center, Cedar Terrace, Cascade View and Gateway. Name yours in the listing, because it tells buyers which schools, roads and stops apply. The city sits on a plateau, and its edges follow Hall Creek and the Interurban Trail on the west, 212th Street Southwest on the north and 39th Avenue West on the east, which helps a buyer picture where your street falls. Public schools belong to the Edmonds School District, which has five schools inside the city.

sections.h2: Permit rules that matter at sale time
sections.html:
Work without a permit is the main risk. The city treats skipping one as a code violation that can bring fines. You may have to obtain permits and pass inspection or restore the site, and fees may be doubled as a penalty.

  • Windows, siding, roofing, plumbing, electrical and structural changes always need a permit.
  • Sheds over 80 square feet or over 6 feet high need one, and a garage turned into living space is a change of use that needs one.
  • Removing drywall and exposing framing needs one, even for a wall removal or remodel.
  • Like-for-like cabinet replacement, painting and carpet do not.
  • Permits expire if work does not start and pass an inspection within 180 days.

An owner doing the work must live in the home, and a contractor is required if you plan to rent or sell. Email permitspecialist@mltwa.gov about a specific project, and check the posted counter hours before you visit.

sections.h2: Excise tax and recording in Snohomish County
sections.html:
The Snohomish County Treasurer reviews the deed first, then the Auditor's Recording Division records it. If tax is owed, recording waits until it is paid in full at the Treasurer's excise tax counter.

That counter is at 3000 Rockefeller Avenue in Everett, open Monday through Friday from 9 a.m. to 3 p.m., phone 425-388-3366. Recording is in the same building, open 9 a.m. to 5 p.m., phone 425-388-3483, and mailed documents need the exact recording fee, which depends on document type and page count.

State tax moves through four bands, from 1.1 percent to 3 percent. The first band ends at $525,000 through December 31, 2026 and at $551,000 from January 1, 2027, and a local rate comes on top. The tax is owed on the sale date, meaning the date of notarization. RCW 64.06.020 also has the seller disclosure statement reach the buyer five business days after mutual acceptance, with exceptions for waivers and exempt transfers.

Electricity comes from Snohomish County Public Utility District and natural gas from Puget Sound Energy. The Alderwood Water and Wastewater District serves water and sewer, and Waste Management collects garbage, recycling and yard waste under city contract. Hand the buyer that list so they can budget monthly bills, and schedule final readings and account transfers a few days before closing so nothing lapses on move-in day. If you are selling a house that was rented, tell the utilities which party holds each account.

After you accept an offer, the title company opens an order and prepares a settlement statement. Sign the deed and the excise tax affidavit, and make sure any tax is paid at the counter in Everett before the Auditor records the deed. Recording fees depend on document type and page count, so ask what to expect. When recording is done, funds are released and you hand over keys.

If the house has an addition or a converted garage, put the permit paperwork in the file early. A buyer's lender is likely to ask about it, and answering quickly keeps the closing date from slipping. On a cash deal the same paperwork still matters, though a buyer who takes the house as it stands may care less about the details.

A cash sale fits when the house needs updating, a probate or move is on a deadline, or you want to skip repairs a buyer's lender would require. Older houses with deferred updates are a typical fit.

Get any buyer to prove funds, fix a closing day in writing, and say who pays excise tax and title fees. Then set the offer beside a listing's net after tax, agent fees, repairs and carrying costs, and request a bid on your address to see both numbers.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Mountlake Terrace house that has unpermitted work?
faqs.a: Yes, but expect it to come up. Work without a permit is a code violation, and you may have to obtain permits and pass inspection or return the site to its original condition. Put your case to the permit specialists before listing, or look for a buyer who accepts the house as it stands.

faqs.q: Who records the deed for a Mountlake Terrace sale?
faqs.a: Snohomish County does. The Treasurer's Office reviews conveyance documents such as deeds for excise tax, and the Auditor's Recording Division records them after any tax is paid. Recording is at 3000 Rockefeller Avenue in Everett, phone 425-388-3483.

faqs.q: How is the excise tax on a Mountlake Terrace sale calculated?
faqs.a: Rates rise in bands from 1.1 percent on the first slice, and a local rate sits on top. Closings in 2027 and later start with higher breakpoints. Your title officer can run the total for your price.

faqs.q: Which school district serves Mountlake Terrace?
faqs.a: The Edmonds School District. Five of its schools are inside the city: one high school, one middle school and three elementary schools. Check your attendance area with the district before an ad names a school.

faqs.q: Does the light rail station affect selling a Mountlake Terrace house?
faqs.a: It gives you a transit selling point. The station has 890 parking stalls and has had Link light rail service since the Lynnwood extension opened in August 2024. Mention the station and the commute time when you describe the house.
